title: Blueprints and Objects
description: Learn Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) by building your own magical creatures using Blueprints (Classes)!

content.value: Imagine you are a toy manufacturer. You don't design every toy car from scratch with unique molds. Instead, you design a single Blueprint, and then stamp out thousands of toy cars from it! In programming, this Blueprint is called a Class, and the stamped-out items are called Objects.
We use the `class` keyword to create our blueprint. Inside, we can set traits (Variables, which we call Attributes) and actions (Functions, which we call Methods).
To create an object from your blueprint class, you write the class name with parentheses and pass the traits!

dog1 = Dog("Buddy", "Golden Retriever")
dog2 = Dog("Max", "Pug")

print(dog1.name)  # Prints Buddy
dog2.bark()       # Prints Max says Woof!
Notice the word `self` in the function parameters? It is a special word Python uses to refer to the current object being created or manipulated!

practice.question: Create a Dog object named 'rover' of breed 'Labrador' (using the Dog class defined above), then call rover.bark()!
